rules.title: Newark municipal rent control / rent leveling ordinance (unverified)
rules.requirement: Newark is believed to have a municipal rent control ordinance limiting rent increases, enforced locally. The captured documents do not give its text, so check the ordinance and the Newark rent control office for the cap and covered units.
rules.citation: Newark Rent Control Ordinance (Newark Mun. Code)
rules.quoted_span: Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.
rules.conflict_note: Unverified: the Newark code text (ecode360 link-only source D070-D072) could not be read. The quoted span is from D067 (NJ DCA Truth in Renting guide), which says only that NJ municipalities may adopt rent control.
rules.review_note: Cap formula, exemptions and section number are unknown. The 30-year new-construction exemption comes from N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5, as described in D067.

parsed.notes: No candidates were given for Newark. The readable documents (D060, D065-D069) describe New Jersey state law only: the FAIR Act, the Fair Chance in Housing Act, the $50 application fee cap, the security deposit law and the Anti-Eviction Act. Those belong at the state level and were not duplicated here. The Newark code sources (D070-D072) are link-only and could not be read. Newark's rent control ordinance is added as an unverified, low-confidence record. I added no no-rule findings: the documents don't show that Newark lacks a rule in any other category. The FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43, §6.b) bars municipalities from enacting ordinances that conflict with it.
